rationale: C13 plausibly supplied a material drafting template. Both memoranda concern private bills seeking income-tax refunds barred by the statutory limitations period, and they follow the same sequence: describe the proposed refund, recount the untimely claim, invoke finality in tax administration, warn of discrimination against similarly situated taxpayers and an undesirable precedent, and withhold approval. The child reproduces C13's concluding policy language nearly verbatim. C15 and C20 are also very close precedents, but C13 has the strongest literal correspondence.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The statutory period of limitations, which Congress has included in the revenue system as a matter of sound policy, is essential for finality in tax administration.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The statutory period of limitations, which the Congress has included in the revenue system as a matter of sound policy, is essential in order to achieve finality in tax administration.
shared_material.explanation: Nearly verbatim statement of the limitations-period policy, with only minor compression.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Granting special relief in this case would discriminate against other taxpayers similarly situated and would create an undesirable precedent.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Granting special relief in this case would constitute a discrimination against other taxpayers similarly situated and would create an undesirable precedent.
shared_material.explanation: Distinctive concluding sentence is reproduced almost word for word.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The records of the Treasury Department show that the taxpayers filed a timely joint income-tax return for 1950 and that, on March 1, 1955, the taxpayers filed an untimely claim for refund
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The taxpayer, in filing her income tax return for 1951 and paying the amount shown on the return, failed to take credit for a previous partial payment of income tax... The taxpayer, however, did not file her claim until about two months later, at which time the statutory period had expired
shared_material.explanation: Both use the same administrative narrative machinery: a tax overpayment, an untimely refund claim, expiration of the three-year limitation, and rejection of individualized relief.
